what_matters.head: September payrolls rose just 29,000; analysts expected about 84,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2%.
what_matters.detail: August was revised down to 133,000 and July to a loss of 10,000. By Monday, futures priced a 22% chance of an October Fed rate hike, down from 64% a week earlier, and still 87% for one by December. The 10-year yield fell to about 5.18% after the release but closed 4bp higher at 5.28%.

what_matters.head: European chip stocks jumped on Friday: Infineon +8.8%, 2.5× its usual day and the only name past 2×.
what_matters.detail: Reuters credited renewed AI enthusiasm, with soft US jobs data and lower oil easing Fed hike bets. The Wall Street Journal tied it to a report that Samsung is raising its memory-chip prices; that report was not found, so its date is unconfirmed.

what_matters.head: Micron's Taiwan union strike vote closes Tuesday 6 Oct.
what_matters.detail: A pass needs yes votes from more than half of all members, and gives the union a right to strike, not a date.

after_data.text: Oil slipped in Asian trade: Middle East crude exports rose above pre-war levels on four of the last seven days of September (shipping data), and the G7 reserve release adds supply. The Houthis said they fired missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and Khurais. Not in Friday's US prices.
The dollar held near a 17-month high as French fiscal worries weighed on the euro; at the run, the dollar index quote was 0.5% above Friday's settle. Not in Friday's US prices.

latest.tape_note: Stocks rose on Friday after the soft jobs report; chips (SOXX) gained 2.2% and Nvidia touched a record intraday high. VIX fell 6.6% to 15.3. Oil fell 1.9% after G7 countries agreed on Friday to release 100 million barrels of crude and diesel from emergency reserves. Gold fell 1.0%, and the US dollar slipped 0.1% against the Singapore dollar.
